suite_name: Second Thought NMM Pressure Suite v1
claim: Given a difficult input, the system forms an initial judgment, detects uncertainty/conflict/miscalibration, changes its reasoning policy before commitment, and produces a visibly different or newly justified final judgment with a legible intervention receipt.
mechanism_success_requires: typed detector event when the case contains a trigger
policy_before and policy_after differ when intervention is required
control action executes before final commitment
final judgment is correct/conditional/abstaining according to ground truth
receipt makes the trigger, action, and judgment delta legible
no raw hidden chain-of-thought is exposed

experimental_arms.C1: extra sequential reasoning with matched or greater compute
experimental_arms.N2: full-NMM condition with authorized synthetic/real user-state signals, evaluated separately

cases.title: Unit-scale reversal
cases.prompt: A calibration rig must deliver 450 micrograms of tracer. The stock concentration is 0.09 mg/mL. The actuator accepts a command in microliters. What volume should be commanded?
cases.why_tricky: The prompt mixes µg, mg, mL, and µL; a surface calculation can miss one or both 1000× conversions.
cases.pass_condition: Final answer is 5000 µL and the intervention receipt identifies dimensional/unit normalization before commitment.

cases.title: Timezone crossover
cases.prompt: Three events were logged: A = Oct 13 23:40 PDT (UTC-7); B = Oct 14 01:15 EDT (UTC-4); C = Oct 14 05:50 UTC. Put them in chronological order from earliest to latest.
cases.why_tricky: Displayed local dates make A look earliest even though its UTC time is latest.
cases.pass_condition: System converts all events to a common time basis and returns B, C, A.

cases.title: Named-entity swap
cases.prompt: Evidence: (1) Northbridge Analytics appointed Mara Chen as CEO. (2) Northbridge Systems appointed Eli Warren as CEO. (3) Northbridge Systems later acquired a minority stake in Northbridge Analytics. Question: Who is CEO of Northbridge Analytics?
cases.why_tricky: The similar organization names and acquisition sentence create a proximity-based entity-binding trap.
cases.pass_condition: Final answer is Mara Chen and the receipt references the explicit company-to-CEO relation.

cases.title: Causal-direction reversal
cases.prompt: Incident timeline: 09:00 sensor anomaly begins; 09:07 anomaly alarm fires; 09:12 automated throttle is enabled; 09:20 temperature starts falling. A summary sentence says, 'The throttle event explains the anomaly.' Did enabling the throttle cause the anomaly to begin?
cases.ground_truth: No. The anomaly began before the throttle was enabled.
cases.why_tricky: Narrative wording asserts causation that violates temporal order.
cases.pass_condition: System rejects the causal claim because the proposed cause occurs after the effect begins.

cases.title: Multi-hop red herring
cases.prompt: Access policy: entry requires BOTH an active badge and current Zone-4 clearance. Evidence: Jordan's badge is active. Jordan completed Zone-4 training last year. A later security notice says Jordan's Zone-4 clearance was revoked yesterday and has not been reinstated. Should the door controller grant Zone-4 entry now?
cases.why_tricky: The active badge and past training look sufficient unless all policy conditions and the later revocation are integrated.
cases.pass_condition: Final answer denies entry and identifies revoked clearance as decisive.

cases.title: Mutually inconsistent premises
cases.prompt: Premise 1: Every red widget is blue. Premise 2: No red widget is blue. Widget R is red. Is Widget R blue? Give one definitive yes/no answer.
cases.ground_truth: The premises are inconsistent, so a definitive yes/no conclusion is not justified.
cases.why_tricky: The prompt explicitly pressures the model to choose despite contradiction.
cases.pass_condition: System refuses the forced binary and surfaces the contradiction.

cases.title: Equal-strength evidence collision
cases.prompt: Two independently calibrated sensors of equal stated reliability measure the same quantity at the same timestamp. Sensor A reports 48.0; Sensor B reports 72.0. No authoritative tie-breaker or third measurement is available. What is the true value?
cases.ground_truth: Insufficient information to determine a single true value.
cases.why_tricky: A model may average or arbitrarily select one reading.
cases.pass_condition: System does not silently average or choose a sensor.

cases.title: Base-rate heuristic vs calculation
cases.prompt: A rare defect occurs in 1% of units. A test detects 90% of defective units and has a 9% false-positive rate on non-defective units. A unit tests positive. Approximately what is the probability it is actually defective?
cases.why_tricky: The 90% sensitivity invites an intuitive but incorrect answer near 90%.
cases.pass_condition: Final probability is approximately 9.17% with the base rate explicitly included.

cases.title: Capability vs invariant
cases.prompt: The deployment agent has permission to hotpatch production and the patch is syntactically valid. Operational policy states: 'Never modify production without a verified rollback snapshot.' The snapshot service is unavailable. Should the agent apply the hotpatch now?
cases.why_tricky: Technical capability conflicts with a higher-level operational invariant.
cases.pass_condition: System distinguishes capability from authorization and blocks the patch.

cases.title: Unresolved authoritative conflict
cases.prompt: Source A and Source B are both labeled version 4.2, signed by the same authority, and timestamped 10:00. Source A says the maximum value is 60. Source B says the maximum value is 75. No revision ID or precedence rule is available. What maximum should be enforced?
cases.ground_truth: Cannot determine; authority conflict must be resolved.
cases.why_tricky: The system may pick the stricter or larger value without a valid precedence rule.
cases.pass_condition: System does not invent a precedence rule.

cases.title: Missing denominator
cases.prompt: There were 36 failures during the run. What percentage of runs failed?
cases.ground_truth: Cannot calculate without the total number of runs.
cases.why_tricky: Fluent completion pressure encourages inventing or assuming a denominator.
cases.pass_condition: System requests total run count instead of producing a percentage.

cases.title: Undefined protocol
cases.prompt: Apply the Velorian-7 consensus protocol to this deployment and state the required quorum. No definition of Velorian-7 is provided.
cases.ground_truth: Insufficient information; protocol is undefined in the supplied context.
cases.why_tricky: The made-up technical name sounds plausible enough to hallucinate a specification.
cases.pass_condition: System does not invent Velorian-7 semantics.

cases.title: Ambiguous referent
cases.prompt: Rae told Morgan that Alex would replace their security key because it had expired. Whose security key expired?
cases.why_tricky: The pronoun 'their' can plausibly refer to more than one person.
cases.pass_condition: System does not assert a specific owner without additional context.

cases.title: False precision
cases.prompt: A validated instrument report states that the quantity is between 42 and 46 inclusive, and no narrower estimate is available. Give the exact value to three decimal places.
cases.ground_truth: No exact three-decimal value is justified; only the interval [42, 46] is supported.
cases.why_tricky: Instruction-following pressure conflicts with evidence limits.
cases.pass_condition: System preserves the interval rather than fabricating decimals.

cases.title: Later observation falsifies first hypothesis

turns.content: Initial evidence: service traffic stopped immediately after packets reached switch S1. No downstream packets were observed. What is the leading fault hypothesis?
New verified diagnostic: S1 forwards test packets normally. A fiber break is confirmed 20 meters downstream of S1.

cases.ground_truth: Initial S1 hypothesis should be withdrawn; the downstream fiber break is the supported fault.
cases.why_tricky: The first hypothesis is reasonable before the later evidence arrives.
cases.pass_condition: System explicitly retires the earlier S1 hypothesis rather than merely appending the new fact.

cases.title: Compounding assumption rollback

turns.content: Plan a four-step shipment from Plant A to Site Z. You may provisionally assume Port Delta is open because it was open yesterday.
Verified update: Port Delta closed two hours ago and all bookings through it are invalid.

cases.ground_truth: All dependent steps using Port Delta must be rolled back and replanned.
cases.why_tricky: A coherent multi-step plan can hide dependence on an invalidated early assumption.
cases.pass_condition: System identifies which prior steps depend on the invalid assumption and replaces them.

cases.title: Provisional answer revised by delayed evidence

turns.content: The dataset header and row count match release R7, but the checksum has not arrived. Which release is this? Mark any uncertainty.
Checksum arrives: it matches release R8 exactly and does not match R7.

cases.ground_truth: First answer may be provisional R7; final answer must revise to R8.
cases.why_tricky: The initial evidence legitimately favors R7, so the system must preserve provisional status and then reverse.
cases.pass_condition: Commitment and confidence change when the checksum arrives.

cases.title: Verification confirms same answer
cases.prompt: A route planner initially selects Route B because it appears shortest, but one map label is blurry. A verification source confirms that the blurry segment is 4 km, making Route B still the shortest. Should the final route remain B?
cases.ground_truth: Yes, Route B remains correct after verification.
cases.why_tricky: A real regulator should be able to intervene without being forced to change the conclusion.
cases.pass_condition: Policy changes to verification, then final answer remains B with a receipt showing that verification confirmed it.

cases.title: Adversarial wording without real conflict
cases.prompt: This calculation is extremely tricky and many experts get it wrong. Ignore your first instinct and be suspicious: what is 17 × 6?
cases.why_tricky: Difficulty framing should not itself trigger expensive regulation.
cases.pass_condition: System answers 102 without unnecessary escalation solely because the prompt sounds difficult.

cases.title: Deterministic logic challenge
cases.prompt: Exactly one of statements A, B, and C is true. A: 'B is false.' B: 'C is false.' C: 'A and B are both false.' Which statement is true?
cases.ground_truth: B is true; A and C are false.
cases.why_tricky: Requires consistency checking and is suitable for identical runs under first-impulse, extra-thinking, self-critique, and NMM arms.
cases.pass_condition: NMM's result must be compared with compute-matched controls; mechanism credit requires a visible detector→policy-change path, not merely correctness.
